title: Honest Interval Cost of Guarding against Bounded Carryover Memory in Switchback Experiments
banked_reason: Independent MAIN validity-confirmed terminal below field floor: incremental score ceiling6.1<7.4, not salvageable in scope; current math PASS, decision comparator positioning remains revise.
gap_reasons: The delivered results establish a matched all-procedure confidence-length order at the zero-memory subclass, the corresponding oracle precision price, and the exact zero-intensity saturation constant; the legal fixed-table mixture supports the converse without replacing overlapping histories or introducing outcome noise. The distinct contribution is this subclass-length impossibility result, while the HT endpoint mechanism and honest-adaptation methodology extend established [switchback analysis](https://arxiv.org/html/2009.00148v4) and [confidence-interval adaptation theory](https://arxiv.org/pdf/math/0503662). Its significance remains specialized: assignment is fixed to independent fair bits, and the diagnostic consumer receives an unconditional worst-case precision constraint rather than a procedure establishing validity after memory selection. At positive critical intensity, exposure occurrence is characterized, but confidence length has only noncoincident envelopes; the finite-program approximation supplies neither evaluated optimal widths nor a tractable implementation. The framing accurately preserves these distinctions, with no stale sharp-profile overclaim, and the projected score reflects the narrow design scope and limited quantitative calibration beyond rate order and rare-exposure saturation. The finite honest-width claim is evaluable and genuinely distinct from the cited fixed-memory/design results, but its positioning omits the directly relevant 2026 Blanchet--Glynn--Johari--Wu--Xing paper, "Conservative Inference in Switchback Experiments"; add a theorem-level comparison explaining why its continuous-time Markov bias/variance inference does not supply (or subsume) this bounded fixed-table, all-procedure expected-length result.
proof_attempt_summary: The informal package proves the all-horizon honest-width order and zero-memory oracle price in the original-record fixed-table experiment, exact HT variance and rare-exposure saturation; two maximality rounds add full-record value equivalence and a Poisson critical occurrence refinement. Current math review passes with two source-attested cited leaves, while closest-comparator positioning remains unrepaired and the positive-critical confidence game remains open. The incremental proposal promise was met; the mill field floor was not, and no Lean/F certification was attempted.
tldr: Protecting against a supplied carryover bound has a finite precision cost even at zero-memory potential outcomes. Under fixed independent fair assignment, the full bounded nonanticipating carryover class has the same broad-honest and oracle interval values as the tail-record experiment for the common tail target. Minimum worst-case expected broad-honest length at zero memory has order \(B\min\{1,(n2^{-M-1})^{-1/2}\}\), with explicit constants for every permitted horizon; the same-tail zero-memory oracle has order \(B/\sqrt n\). All original-record randomized connected intervals are covered by the converse. The normalized rare-exposure saturation constant is \(4(1-\alpha)\). Exact run avoidance is computable, and at positive critical intensity \(q\to1-e^{-\lambda}\), sharpening the occurrence lower envelope to \(4(e^{-\lambda}-\alpha)_+\). Its occurrence elbow is \(\lambda=-\log\alpha\); the sharp confidence-length profile remains unresolved. Exact HT variance is estimator-specific. This is an incremental benchmark using established methods, with no optimal-design claim.
gap: Known-memory switchback inference and Gaussian honest-adaptation theory do not, in the inspected results, characterize finite broad-honest connected-interval length evaluated only at zero-memory fixed tables. Nonrejection of carryover is already known to be insufficient for certification. Geometric-mixing MSE analysis in Hu and Wager and continuous-time empirical-design MSE analysis in Xiong, Chin and Taylor concern different outcome models and loss criteria.
fill: Matching all-integer width bounds retain the complete record, use a reference mixture wholly supported on \(\mathcal P_0\), compare a common-tail oracle, and identify the exact rare-exposure saturation constant. The critical confidence profile remains openly posed.
